# Freeze store integrity maintenance

Ensure the `TextFileBasedViolationStore` maintains the integrity of its `stored.rules` index and files.

Setting `default.integrity` to `repair` will check the index and folder as they are on disk during initialization, even if the same folder was initialized before. Defaulting to `ignore` which checks nothing.

If an entry points to a path that is not a regular file directly within the folder, it is broken. This also applies if the file name is not a valid path.

If an entry is not broken and its file has no violations it is resolved. Files that only contain line breaks are also resolved.

Entries that point to the same file name are shared, even if nothing exists with that name. If multiple entries point to the same regular file they are also shared. Including through a symbolic or hard link. Even if that file is outside the folder.

The `TextFileBasedViolationStore` will not touch any shared entries or files that no entry points to. If an entry is shared and anything else it will remain shared.

When set to `repair` broken entries will be discarded without touching whatever they point to.

When set to `repair` resolved entries and the file they point to will be discarded. If a resolved entry is a symbolic link the file it points to will be deleted as well.

If using `repair` and saving no violations for a known rule it will forget the rule. Its entry will be removed and its file as well. Unless another entry is sharing that file. In which case only the entry will be removed. Even if it points outside the folder. If using `repair` and saving no violations for an unknown rule nothing will be saved.

If it cannot delete the file of a rule it is forgetting it will fail to save and leave the entry.

steps.message:
`TextFileBasedViolationStore` now has the `default.integrity` setting (`ignore` by default, or `repair`), and the freeze tests pass: 78 tests, including 19 new ones. The full `archunit` suite (15,824 tests) passed before my last change; after it I only re-ran the freeze tests. I couldn't run Spotless or SpotBugs because their dependencies aren't in the offline Gradle cache.

**How `repair` behaves**
- **On every initialization** it re-reads `stored.rules` from disk, even if the folder was initialized before. This matters because `FreezingArchRule` re-initializes the store on every rule evaluation, so with `repair` the whole folder is checked each time a frozen rule runs.
- **Broken entries** are removed from the index. The file name must be a plain name of a regular file directly in the folder; missing files, folders, dangling links, `sub/x`, `../x`, absolute paths and invalid names all count as broken. Nothing they point to is touched.
- **Resolved entries** (file is empty or contains only `\n`/`\r`) are removed and their file is deleted. If the file is a symbolic link, the file it points to is deleted too, even outside the folder.
- **Shared entries** are never touched: entries with the same file name, or pointing to the same regular file through symbolic or hard links. Files that no entry points to are also left alone.
- **Saving no violations** for a known rule removes its entry and deletes its file, unless the file is shared (then only the entry goes). For an unknown rule nothing is saved. If the file can't be deleted, the save fails and the entry stays.

**Choices I made where the spec was silent**
- **`repair` with `allowStoreUpdate=false`:** initialization fails, but only if there is actually something to repair, so a store marked read-only is never changed silently.
- **Deletion fails during initialization:** the store logs a warning and keeps the entry instead of failing. Only a failed save is an error, as the spec says.
- **Sharing is checked against every entry's target, including broken entries.** So `../outside/f` and a link to the same file count as shared and are both kept. I chose the cautious side because a shared entry must never be touched.
- **A missing `stored.rules` is recreated** if it was deleted after the folder was first initialized, the same way a first-time initialization would.
- **An unrecognised value for `default.integrity`** makes initialization fail with an error listing `ignore, repair`.
